_evidence_source: synthetic: romance-scam-style variant combining a secrecy demand with an unexplained recipient relationship — a distinct red-flag combination from fixtures 13-15 (which pair secrecy+urgency, urgency+irreversible-payment, and unexplained-relationship+irreversible-payment respectively), modeled on the FTC-documented pattern where a supposed online partner asks the victim to keep the payment secret from family (see references/scam-red-flags.md)

call.task: Verify a flagged $9,200 wire transaction to an individual the account holder met online.
call.summary: Account holder reported being asked to keep the payment secret from family and could not confirm the recipient's identity beyond messages exchanged online.

attempts.summary: Account holder confirmed secrecy demand and could not explain the recipient relationship.

transcript_turns.speaker: bot
transcript_turns.text: This is an automated verification call from your bank about a flagged transaction. Did anyone ask you to keep this transaction private?

transcript_turns.speaker: user
transcript_turns.text: Yes, he asked me not to mention it to my kids, said they wouldn't understand.

transcript_turns.speaker: bot
transcript_turns.text: Is there time pressure on this payment?

transcript_turns.speaker: user
transcript_turns.text: Not really, he said whenever I could send it was fine.

transcript_turns.speaker: bot
transcript_turns.text: Can you describe your relationship to the recipient, in your own words?

transcript_turns.speaker: user
transcript_turns.text: We met on a dating site about two months ago, we've only spoken online and by phone, I've never met him in person.

transcript_turns.speaker: bot
transcript_turns.text: Were you asked to pay by wire, gift card, or cryptocurrency specifically?

transcript_turns.speaker: user
transcript_turns.text: Wire, he said it was for a business emergency overseas.
